about: Thresholds, word lists and matching rules for the Engagement media and reusable content cleanup. scripts/media_library_audit.py reads this file and its CLI defaults come from it; change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes, and references/checks.md says what each finding means.

notes.large_image_bytes: An image file larger than this many bytes slows email and page loads on mobile connections: a medium finding when live content uses it, low otherwise.
notes.huge_image_bytes: An image larger than this many bytes is a high finding when live content uses it (medium otherwise). Engagement's own import limit for images is 2 MB.
notes.max_image_width_px: An image wider or taller than this many pixels is far beyond what an email (usually 600 to 1,200 pixels wide at double density) or a weblayer needs: a low finding. Resize it before use.
notes.tracking_pixel_max_px: Images whose width and height attributes are both at most this many pixels are tracking pixels and spacers, so they're not checked for alt text.
notes.stale_days: An unused file or asset created (or last edited) more than this many days ago goes on the delete list; a newer unused one is listed for review, because someone may be about to use it.
notes.min_duplicate_bytes: Files smaller than this many bytes aren't matched as duplicates by size and dimensions alone (icons and spacers often share sizes). Files with the same name and the same size are always matched.
notes.min_copy_text_chars: An SMS template whose message text is at least this long, and appears word for word in an SMS campaign or scenario, is reported as copied into that message. Shorter texts aren't matched.
notes.live_statuses: Statuses (compared case-insensitively) that count as live for a campaign, scenario, weblayer or in-app message. Draft, inactive, paused and finished ones count as drafts; archived ones don't count.
notes.required_usage_kinds: The kinds of content that must be searched before a file, block or snippet can be called unused. If one wasn't loaded, or returned 403, unused items are 'unused (unverified)' instead.
notes.content_asset_kinds: Reusable content that campaigns reference by ID ({{ block('<id>') }}, {{ snippet('<id>') }}), so a file used inside one counts as used wherever the block or snippet is used. Their details must be loaded for files inside them to be found.
notes.template_kinds: Saved templates (email, SMS and app inbox) that are copied into a campaign when used, not referenced, so no tool shows where they were used. They're 'not traceable' rather than unused, and a file used only inside one is 'template only'.
notes.alt_text_kinds: Kinds of content whose images are checked for alt text (email designs, in campaigns, scenario email steps, blocks and email templates).
notes.test_name_words: Whole words in a file or asset name that suggest a test, placeholder or throwaway copy.
notes.name_noise_patterns: Regular expressions (case-insensitive) removed from a name before names are compared for duplicates: the content hash and extension that template imports add, 'copy of', '(1)', '-copy' and trailing version numbers. Applied in order.
notes.max_usage_details_before_asking: If more campaign, scenario, weblayer and in-app message details than this would have to be fetched with designs, say how many calls that is and ask before going on (or offer live ones first).
notes.max_directories_before_asking: If the file library has more folders than this to browse, say how many calls that is and ask before going on.
notes.max_users_listed: At most this many users (campaigns, scenarios and so on) are listed per file or asset; the rest are counted.
